findings.finding: No valuation was executed, so the table has no fair value or scenario prices and none of the three scenario stories has been priced. Blocker 1 is a data error that the engine read correctly as a conflict: dataqa cash_and_liquid_investments = 4,588.3M = cash 2,288.3M + 'short_term_investments' 2,300.0M. The 10-Q of 2026-08-10 (reading/10q_2026-08-10.txt, fair-value note near line 2992) says the ~$2.3B is money-market cash equivalents INSIDE cash and cash equivalents, so it is counted twice. Spendable cash is 2,288.3M; the 434.6M of restricted cash (UBS loan collateral 428.4M plus 6.2M) stays out. The analyst flagged this double count in position.json gaps[0] and understand/business.json flags.
findings.where: companies/ASTS/out/casefile.json qa.fields.cash_and_liquid_investments (status conflict, blocking) and rv.mechanical.dataqa_blocking; source fact pf_short_term_investments (companyfacts CashEquivalents tag mapped as short-term investments)
findings.fix: Repair: set an inputs override of cash_and_liquid_investments = 2,288,253,000 at 2026-06-30 with short_term_investments = 0, citing nm_cash_q_2026_06_30 and pf_10q_20260810 (the cash-equivalents note), then rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: Blocker 2, separate from the cash error: the forecast is method_not_supported_by_forecast, 'cash-cost ratio outside driver bounds (operating losses above 100% of revenue)'. The FY2025 operating margin is -400% to -600%, so even with the cash fixed the scenario_survival_fcff path will not build. Contributing data error: auto.json and the prefetch use pf_operating_income_fy2025 = -425.3M, but the 10-K gives -287.7M (revenue 70.9M less opex 358.6M; nm_operating_income_fy2025). That puts the history margin at -5.997 instead of about -4.06.
findings.where: casefile.json fc.status / fc.reason and val.status; understand/auto.json history operating margin FY2025; pf_operating_income_fy2025
findings.fix: Repair: override FY2025 operating income to -287.7M (nm_operating_income_fy2025). Then start the forecast from a pre-service build path (the current_year_revenue guidance of 150-200M with the guided opex of ~100M a quarter plus SBC) using the engine's start-up / pre-revenue route if one exists. If no supported route exists, the result stays a visible draft with no price. Do not loosen the bounds by inventing margins.

findings.finding: Counter-thesis (pre-mortem, November 2029: the investment failed). Constellation: ASTS reached roughly 45-60 BlueBirds a year or more late because of launch scarcity. Its main launch provider is SpaceX, which is also its main competitor; New Glenn failed in May 2026 and BB7 was lost. Competition: by then Starlink Mobile, live with T-Mobile on its own EchoStar AWS-4/H-block spectrum and 11,000+ satellites (SpaceX E&G revenue $5.04B in 9M 2026, +70%), was the default direct-to-device layer. The AT&T/Verizon/T-Mobile JV of 2026-10-02 used ASTS as a second source and squeezed the undisclosed revenue share. Money: service revenue arrived late and small (only 6.6% of the 1.2B RPO falls within 12 months). Opex kept running above guide (raised from 70-80M to ~100M a quarter and beaten twice), SBC ran at ~250M a year, and each slip was funded by more converts or equity on top of the ~3.7B of convert principal. Economic shares had already grown from 256M (FY2025 average diluted) to 389M. Ligado approvals stalled in the Inmarsat litigation, tying up the 520M paid. The stock fell to a value set by the cost of the network, not by service cash flows. What would have shown it early: (a) no BlueBird launch confirmed between 2026-08-10 and 2026-11-01, and fewer than 30 in orbit by mid-2027; (b) no SpaceMobile service revenue line in the 10-Q for Q2 2027; (c) a revenue-share percentage disclosed below the level implied by consensus, or carriers routing JV traffic to Starlink; (d) another convert or ATM before service launch, or economic shares above 450M; (e) Q3 or Q4 2026 opex above 115M a quarter.
findings.fix: Keep this as the counter-thesis behind the scenes. Add falsifiers (d) and (a) as numeric bear triggers (see the falsifier finding).

findings.finding: The economics-mode path borrows Iridium's operating margin (27.1%/27.4%/16.9%) but not Iridium's capital intensity. Iridium earns those margins on a network whose sales to invested capital is far below 0.6-1.5, so its own return on capital is single digits. The path's ROICs of 14% (base) and 25% (bull) come from pairing Iridium's peak margin with ASTS's guided build cost (21-23M a satellite for about 90 satellites). Two more gaps: (1) no replacement capex for LEO satellites, and nothing for expansion toward the 248-satellite FCC authorization; (2) no evidence of capacity per satellite to show that 90 satellites can carry 2.7B (base) or 3.4B (bull) of revenue. The bull's 25% is labelled 'unproven' correctly, but it is a cherry-picked combination, not a competitor reading. ASTS's own ROIC record runs from -27% to -179% (prefetch/forensic.json).
findings.where: position.json company_path.scenarios.base.roic (0.14) and bull.roic (0.25); drivers.sales_to_capital base 1.0 / bull 1.5; drivers.mature_margin
findings.fix: Analyst path: compute IRDM's own ROIC (NOPAT / invested capital) from pf_peer_IRDM and use it as the competitor anchor for the base, or justify the gap with ASTS-specific capacity evidence. Add a replacement-capex term (satellite life from the 10-K) to the capital base. Unless capacity per satellite is evidenced, cap the bull ROIC at a level the evidenced build supports.

findings.finding: The bear changes growth, margin and capital efficiency but sizes none of its own named mechanisms. (1) Ligado: the 520M paid and the 550M Sound Point facility (conditional on approvals; availability to 2026-10-05 plus an extension whose election is not confirmed) are not in the bear's capital or funding. (2) The carrier JV and Starlink: no revenue-share cut is sized. (3) Funding: financing is 'assumed', so the engine raises on its own rule; the convert terms (conversion 72-149 USD against a 40.9 price) mean the 2034 and 2036 notes stay debt, not equity, in a bear, and no refinancing or debt-service stress is modelled. (4) The 2034 1.625% notes (1.15B, issued ~2026-07-20) and their cash are not in the opening balance (post_period_events missing; convertibles missing in dataqa). The bear still reaches ~0.9-1.0B of revenue by 2031 with service; a bear with no service, or a forced-dilution bear, is absent.
findings.where: position.json drivers (bear), forecast_options.financing = assumed, scenario_events.bear[3] (Ligado); casefile qa.fields.convertibles / post_period_events (missing)
findings.fix: Core/repair: add the July 2026 convert issue and its cash as a post-statement event in the capital bridge, using the instrument list from the pack notes (about 3.70B principal with conversion prices). Size Ligado in the bear (520M lost to the backstop route or delayed). Make the bear funding explicit (a raise amount and price, or the share count the bear needs).

findings.finding: The base is anchored to sell-side consensus shifted by one year (FY2027 ~440M, FY2030 ~2.27B), and the bull is consensus itself. The unit economics behind both (MNO revenue-share percentage, ARPU, paid capacity per satellite) are undisclosed (position.json gaps). So beyond FY2027, base and bull are expectations, not company evidence. Base and bull margins are almost the same (0.27 vs 0.274), so the bull differs from the base only in timing and growth.
findings.fix: State next to the result that the revenue beyond FY2027 rests on attributed consensus with undisclosed unit economics. Either evidence a bull margin or capacity mechanism, or say plainly that the bull is the base delivered on time.

findings.finding: Coherence between parts: the base satellite timing differs. analyst_field's base has ~45 satellites in early 2027; core's base has mid-2027, one or two quarters after the target. The field base also calls ASTS a second supplier 'without a clear advantage', which sits uneasily with base economics at Iridium's full margin (27%) and an ROIC of 14%.
findings.where: position/field.json potential base reading vs position/core.json scenario_events.base[1]; company_path.scenarios.base
findings.fix: Align the field base timing to mid-2027 (core). Either lower the base margin toward the second-source reading or explain why a second source earns Iridium's margin.

findings.finding: The falsifiers miss the two fastest early signals of failure, funding and launch cadence: there is no falsifier on economic share count or new convert/equity issuance, and none on launches before mid-2027. The bear falsifier (FY2027 revenue above 450M) cannot be judged until 2028-03-15.
findings.fix: Add: 'economic shares outstanding above 450M by 2027-08-15' (bear confirms / base refuted), and 'BlueBirds in orbit at 2026-12-31 below 20 by 2027-03-15' (base and bull refuted).

findings.finding: Red-team and expectation_gap could not run on substance: redteam_audit returns unable_to_verify (revenue_basis, reinvestment and funding are critical-unverified because there is no driver spec or valuation), and expectation_gap has no valuation case (casefile val not_computed). What the 40.9 price assumes is therefore unknown in this attempt. A 389M-share economic count gives a market cap of about 15.9B, which needs roughly the consensus (bull) path at full margins to justify.
findings.fix: After the repair runs the valuation, rerun redteam_audit and expectation_gap. Show the result as a draft until both pass.
